name: Finite homomorphic images of non-finite systems
description: Exercise 4.69: prove the following assertion or find a counterexample: if Z1 is a finite system and Z2 is not a finite system, then Z1 is not a homomorphic image of Z2. The assertion is false; a counterexample is given.

elements.text: Collapsing every state of the ℕ-counter onto the single state of the one-state system is a homomorphism.
The one-state system is finite, the counter is not finite, and the one-state system is a homomorphic image of the counter.
The stated assertion does not hold.
